extracted.intended_audience: grant writers, grants coordinators, research administrators, and organizational leaders involved in preparing collaborative Federal grant proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Strategies and best-practice criteria for organizing and managing group dynamics and tasks when multiple organizations collaboratively prepare federal grant proposals, with attention to the phases of pre-collaboration, orientation, conflict, emergence, and reinforcement. Emphasizes leadership, coordination, communication, document management, role assignment, budgeting, and debriefing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal planning (pre-collaboration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal planning that takes place well before proposal development and writing; bringing together a core internal team (grant writer(s), program staff, subject experts) to develop agreement on how the organization will respond to an anticipated RFP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes formal strategic planning, discussions to determine fit of opportunity, informal planning of collective approach, obtaining leadership buy-in, reviewing full scope of resources (monetary and staff time), vetting potential obligations with leadership, and anticipating strategies for future conflict (e.g., budget negotiation approaches). Planning equips representatives to articulate organizational contributions and avoid passing up opportunities due to lack of preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing partners / partner selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Determining which external organizations to invite as grant partners based on fit, complementary services/resources, and RFP-mandated partner types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider mandated partner types in the RFP but exercise discretion among entities that could fulfill those roles (e.g., choose among multiple non-profits). Evaluate partners' resources, mission compatibility, history/relationships, community politics, and how each organization's contributions will weave into a comprehensive project. Selection affects group composition, trust-building needs, and negotiation dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positioning the organization for collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Fully understanding the organizational mission, available resources, and the funding environment to strategically position the organization for partnership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop insight through internal planning and networking, assess community need relative to the organization, and be prepared to articulate how the organization's services/resources contribute to a collective approach. This informs what the organization can commit during negotiations and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing the lead applicant / fiscal agent
rubrics_metrics.description: Deciding which organization will act as lead applicant (fiscal agent) because it affects assigned roles, responsibilities, authority, and who prepares/submits the final proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead applicant selection influences who assumes leadership and coordination roles, who has authority over budgets and approvals, and the accountability structure for submission and post-award implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group composition and explicit role definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Define a clear breakdown of group roles and associated tasks (e.g., leader, coordinator, writers, program staff, subject experts) and ensure roles align with organizational hierarchy and responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roles should be assigned based on skills and authority levels; specify tasks tied to each role, clarify who makes final decisions, and prevent diffusion of responsibility by making expectations explicit. Consider hierarchical influence in partner organizations when assigning roles to avoid conflict about authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership characteristics and competencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaders should possess interpersonal and emotional competencies — self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy, and social skills — and be able to both manage projects and lead people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leadership quality may ultimately determine group success even when best practices are used. Select leaders based on current skill level and provide professional development opportunities to strengthen leadership aptitudes. Leaders deploy interpersonal strategies to maintain cohesion, ensure engagement, and address conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinator role and coordinated project management
rubrics_metrics.description: Appoint a coordinator responsible for technical/project-management tasks: circulating work plans, monitoring writing and revisions, tracking timelines, and ensuring tasks are completed on schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The coordinator and leader should work together: the coordinator focuses on task achievement and alerts the leader when interpersonal intercession is needed. This division allows the leader to manage group dynamics while the coordinator enforces follow-through and logistical details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing a work plan and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a work plan and timeline with milestones, meeting dates, deliverables, and task assignments to guide the writing process and meet strict RFP deadlines (often 30–45 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A shared work plan helps negotiate tasks and timelines among partners, reduces diffusion of responsibility, and provides a mechanism for monitoring progress. It should be distributed and updated by the coordinator and referenced in meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication plan (attributes and implementation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design and document an effective communication plan addressing modes of communication, frequency, points of contact, and procedures for circulating drafts and decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attributes include clarity about who communicates what to whom, chosen technologies/modes, regular check-ins, protocols for decision-making and information-sharing, and contingency plans. Effective communication plans set the tone in initial meetings and support transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document management and shared document production
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish methods for shared document production, version control, draft circulation, and referencing specific portions of the document during collaborative editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide on document modes/technology (e.g., shared drives, versioning tools), select a method for distributing draft versions, set naming/version conventions, and ensure everyone knows how to refer to and comment on specific text to avoid duplication and merge errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting collaboration technology appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose technologies and tools (communication and document) that fit the task requirements and the group's capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider task requirements, media choice, and tailoring to group needs; match technology to help coordinate conversation, circulate drafts, and maintain a shared understanding of project requirements and facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigning tasks clearly and preventing diffusion of responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign specific writing and non-writing tasks to named individuals so responsibilities are explicit and equitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address fairness and differences in skills when dividing tasks; ensure people understand expectations and deadlines. Explicit assignments reduce inequitable division of labor and ensure accountability for each component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensuring alignment across proposal sections (coherence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure program description, goals/objectives, activities, budget, and evaluation are coherent and clearly tied together so costs match action items and outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers must weave need, objectives, implementation costs, and evaluation methods into a seamless narrative. Cross-checking and integrated reviews help prevent discrepancies between descriptive sections and budget/evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget negotiation and tying costs to activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Negotiate budgets transparently among partners and ensure each activity is matched to appropriate implementation costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss organizational resource commitments during pre-collaboration; plan for budget negotiations during emergence. Ensure partner contributions (monetary or in-kind) are accounted for and aligned with work plans and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict identification and resolution strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate and address common causes of conflict (e.g., differing missions, hierarchies, influence, agendas) using explicit resolution strategies such as mediation, negotiation, and leadership intervention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect examples of prior unresolved/resolved conflicts to inform strategies; leaders may deploy interpersonal approaches to mediate, set norms, renegotiate roles, or escalate to formal mechanisms. Anticipating conflict during pre-planning can aid quicker resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiating hierarchies, roles, and authority among partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage differing organizational hierarchies and levels of influence so task assignments and decision authority are accepted and adhered to by all partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify who has decision-making authority on particular issues (e.g., budgets, program design), and assign roles in ways that respect partner organizational constraints and reputations to lessen dissension over tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergence-phase strategies for refining the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: In the emergence phase, focus on finalizing goals/objectives, program development details, evaluation plans, budgets, and integrating partner inputs into a cohesive final draft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use coordinated revision cycles, assign finalization tasks, ensure clarity and consistency across sections, and have the coordinator manage final drafts for review. Confirm that partners approve final language and budget allocations prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debriefing practices (formal and informal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct post-project debriefing to create closure, reinforce camaraderie, and capture lessons learned; formal debriefs assess what went well and what to change for future collaborations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although groups often skip formal debriefing, it is recommended for internal teams and ideally for all partner organizations. Debriefing topics include process improvements, partnership viability, implementation plans, and suggestions for future collaborations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building trust and managing interpersonal relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Intentionally build trust among partners, negotiate loyalties and agendas, and manage community politics to create positive working conditions for collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use early meetings to set tone, encourage transparency, address potential ideological differences, and engage in relationship-building activities. Trust reduces friction during conflict and promotes smoother project development and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing shared rhetorical goals and common factual understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop shared rhetorical goals (common objectives, tone, and audience framing) and a mutual understanding of the facts and evidence that underpin the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure group members agree on the problem statement, evidence base, desired outcomes, and key messages. Use coordinated information collection and internal vetting to create a consistent narrative across the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of structured meetings and setting the initial tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Use initial meetings with clear agendas to introduce team members, set goals/objectives, assign roles, and establish norms for ongoing interaction and decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial orientation meetings should set the tone for future collaboration by clarifying expectations, communication protocols, timelines, and roles. Regular, agenda-driven meetings help sustain momentum and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting participants for collaborative capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose participants who bring necessary skills, knowledge, attitudes, and experience to support collaborative capacity and specialized tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider individuals’ collaborative skills and ability to build relationships beyond technical competence. Include those who can represent organizational interests and access resources needed for project development and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership development and ongoing professional learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Invest in leadership development to improve leaders’ capacity for managing interpersonal dynamics and guiding collaborative projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide external or in-house training to strengthen leaders’ self-awareness, self-regulation, empathy, social skills, and project leadership capabilities. Continuous development improves retention, productivity, and team performance.
